sections.title: Problem Statement, Scope and Requirements (URL Shortener)

pages.title: Problem Statement, Scope and Requirements (URL Shortener)

items: {green:In scope}: ==create short link==, ==redirect==, ==custom alias==, ==expiry==, ==click analytics==
{red:Out of scope}: user auth UI
Out of scope: link previews
Out of scope: spam ML
Default TTL when none is given: ==5 years==
Redirect latency: ==p99 under 50 ms==
Read availability: ==99.99%== on redirects
Immutability: a created link ==never changes target==
Reads matter more than writes: a slow or failing redirect breaks every link ever shared

blocks.title: Size the cache from daily traffic
blocks.text: Hot set = 20% of **daily redirects** (70M x 500 B = ==35 GB==), not 20% of all stored links, which would be 600 GB.

rows: Source of truth, `short_code` is the PK
Click events, off the redirect path

spec.title: Write path: POST /v1/urls, about 400/s at peak
Read path: GET /{code}, about 40,000 QPS at peak

items: Reads run at ==100x== writes (100:1), so one shared fleet over-provisions one side
Split into a {green:read service} and a {blue:write service}, each with its own autoscaling
A write spike or deploy never slows redirects
The write service owns the ID generator and primary DB access
Any node can serve ==any code==: the state is in Redis and the DB
So horizontal scaling needs ==no sticky sessions==; the LB uses round robin
A dead node loses nothing; the LB drops it after a failed health check
Peak 40,000 QPS at ~4,000 QPS per node needs about 10 API nodes

blocks.title: Stateless rules
items: No per-user session on a node
Shared state only in Redis, DB, ID generator
Config from env vars, not local files
Expose a health check endpoint for the LB

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Reads are ==100x== writes: split the services, keep every node {red:stateless}, and never put the analytics queue on the redirect path.

sections.title: Short Code Generation: Base62 and Length (URL Shortener)

pages.title: Short Code Generation: Base62 and Length (URL Shortener)

items: Base62 alphabet: ==0-9, a-z, A-Z== = **62 symbols** per character
Avoid base64's `+` and `/`: {red:URL-unsafe}, they need escaping
Codes must be {green:unique}, {blue:short}, and non-guessable if links are private

rows: Too tight for 6B URLs plus retries

items: 6B URLs use about 0.17% of 62^7: {green:large headroom}
7 chars stays short enough for QR codes and SMS
ID 125: 125 = 2x62 + 1, so remainders are 1 then 2
Reversed, the code is =='21'==

blocks.title: Sequential base62 leaks
items: Neighbouring codes reveal **creation order**
The newest code reveals total **volume**
Attackers can enumerate every private link
Fix: random-looking keys, not raw counters

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Unique, short, and unguessable pull against each other: a plain counter is unique and short but ==predictable==.

items: Track the {blue:code length distribution}
Track {purple:keyspace used %} of 62^7
{red:Alert at 50%} of 62^7 used

sections.title: Code Strategies: Counter vs Hash vs Random (URL Shortener)

pages.title: Code Strategies: Counter vs Hash vs Random (URL Shortener)

items: ==Hash==: MD5 or SHA-256 of the long URL, keep the first **7 base62 chars**
{green:Stateless}: any API server computes the same code for the same URL
{red:Collisions grow} past ~==1M links== (birthday bound on 7 chars)
Same long URL gives the same code, so it is **dedup-friendly**
On insert, check the DB for the code
On conflict, ==append a salt or counter== to the URL and rehash
Cost: **one extra read per write**
==Counter==: global auto-increment ID, encoded to base62
{green:Zero collisions}: every ID is unique by construction
{red:Needs a distributed counter}: a single one is a bottleneck and a SPOF
{red:Guessable}: next code is the previous one plus 1
==KGS==: keys are generated **offline**, all unique, 7 chars
Two tables: {green:unused} keys and {red:used} keys
An API server fetches a batch of ==1,000 keys== into memory
Keys are moved to used on handout, so no two servers share one
Codes look random, so they are not guessable
A crashed server wastes ==at most its unused block== of 1M IDs
Waste is tiny against the 3.52T keyspace of 62^7

blocks.note: a duplicate code makes the insert fail, so the app retries

blocks.title: Random without a guard
blocks.text: Picking ==random 7 chars== with no unique constraint silently overwrites or duplicates codes. The **unique index on short_code** is the final collision guard.

items: Look up ==long URL== by code, reply with a **3xx** and a `Location` header
{red:Unknown} code → ==404==
{orange:Expired} code → ==410 Gone==, not 404

rows: Not cached, every click hits you

items: Analytics and expiry needed → ==302== (or **307**), or a 301 with a short private `max-age` as Bitly does
Pure-SEO permanent links → ==301==
`Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` on a 301 keeps clicks reaching you

blocks.note: temporary redirect: every click is counted

blocks.title: 301 is hard to undo
blocks.text: A wrongly-cached permanent redirect with a long `max-age` stays in browsers for ==months==. You cannot recall it, so never ship a long 301 `max-age` for links you may change or expire.

sections.title: Custom Aliases and Link Expiry (URL Shortener)

pages.title: Custom Aliases and Link Expiry (URL Shortener)

q1.text: expires_at set and in the past?

items: {orange:Lazy expiry}: check `expires_at` on **every read**, return ==410==
No timer per link; an expired row costs nothing until it is read
{blue:Daily batch job} deletes expired rows and ==recycles the keys==
Batch is cleanup only; correctness comes from the read check

rows: ==PK==, unique index; holds alias or generated code

items: About ==500 bytes== per row
Alias and generated code share **one** unique index on `short_code`
Insert-or-fail is ==atomic==: no check-then-insert race

blocks.note: let the unique index decide, never SELECT first

rows: Alias breaks the rules or is reserved

items: Length ==4-30== chars
Charset `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`
**Case-sensitive**: `Sale` and `sale` are different codes
Reserved words blocked: `api`, `admin`, `login`

blocks.title: No check-then-insert
blocks.text: A SELECT before the INSERT lets both users pass. The ==unique constraint== is the only guard: one wins, the other gets **409**.

items: ==Never write analytics on the redirect path==
Redirect returns first, then **publishes** a click event to Kafka
Event: `{code, ts, ip, user_agent, referrer}`
Publish is ==asynchronous==: the redirect never waits for Kafka
Consumers aggregate into ==ClickHouse==
Counts per **code** per **minute**, **country**, **device**

blocks.note: returns total clicks, clicks by day, top countries, top referrers

blocks.title: Failure: Kafka down
items: Redirects must ==keep working==
Fire-and-forget into a **bounded buffer**
Buffer full: drop the event, never block
Accept ==losing some clicks==
Event lag under ==10 s==
**Drop rate** of events from the bounded buffer
Consumer throughput vs 40,000/s peak
Bot traffic **filtered** by `user_agent`

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Analytics is ==best-effort==: a lost click is acceptable, a slow or failed redirect is **not**.

items: Key is the ==short code==, value is the `long_url`
On miss: read the DB, then ==SET with a TTL==
{green:Writes also populate the cache}: a new link is hot at once
Target: ==95%+ hit ratio==, miss path under ==10 ms== DB read

blocks.note: hit returns the URL; on miss, fill with an EX TTL

rows: one Redis cluster, 3 shards (~12 GB each)

items: Policy: `maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` evicts the coldest keys
Per-key TTL = ==min(default TTL, time to link expiry)==
A cached link must never outlive its `expires_at`

rows: Viral link key expires, thousands miss at once
==Request coalescing== or a lock: one request refills
Attacker hits random codes, every one misses

blocks.title: Protect the DB
blocks.text: Everything else waits on the ==one refill== for a stampede, and a scan hits the ==negative key== for 60 s instead of the DB.

items: Add a ==CDN or edge cache== in front of Redis
Cache 301s, and only hot 302 targets with a short TTL
Edge hits never reach the API, so redirect p99 stays under 50 ms
Cached edge entries cannot be revoked at once: keep TTL short

blocks.title: Cache targets
items: Hit ratio above ==95%==
Miss path: DB read under ==10 ms==
Negative cache TTL: ==60 s==
Cache size: ==35 GB== on 3 shards
Only query: ==lookup by `short_code`== returns `long_url`
No joins, no range scans, no secondary reads on the hot path
{green:NoSQL} (DynamoDB, Cassandra) and {blue:sharded SQL} both fit
Writes: about ==400/s== at 10x peak; reads: about 40,000 QPS peak
Shard key = ==hash(short_code)== placed on a **consistent hashing** ring
Hashing spreads load evenly: no range hot spots from {red:sequential IDs}
Adding a shard moves only a slice of keys, not everything
==Async read replicas== serve redirects
Primary takes **writes only**, about 400/s at peak
Async copy keeps the write path fast, but replicas can ==lag==
Replica lag: a ==fresh link can 404== on a replica not yet updated
Fix: **read the primary right after create**, replicas for everything else

blocks.title: Fresh link 404
blocks.text: Created links must work at once. After `POST`, the first reads go to the ==primary==, never a lagging replica.

items: Replication lag under ==1 s==
Shard size skew: biggest vs average shard
Disk usage per node: stay near ~50%, alert before it fills
p99 query latency: miss path under 10 ms

sections.title: Scaling, Failures, Trade-offs and Interview Questions (URL Shortener)

pages.title: Scaling, Failures, Trade-offs and Interview Questions (URL Shortener)

items: Peak ==40,000 QPS== / 4,000 QPS per node = about {green:10 API nodes}
Stateless nodes: add or remove freely, no sticky sessions
Sharding is last: ~3 TB in 5 years needs ~6 shards at ~50% fill (3 is the bare minimum)
{blue:Reads}: ==active-active== in every region, each with a regional cache
{orange:Writes}: go to a ==home region==
Each region owns its own ==key range==, so IDs never clash

blocks.title: Abuse controls
items: Rate limit creation: ==100 URLs/hour== per user
Scan target URLs against malware and phishing lists
Block redirect loops: reject targets that point at the shortener's own domain
**Avoid collisions at 100M/month?** KGS or 1M-ID counter blocks; unique index on `short_code` is the last guard
**Count clicks without slowing redirects?** Fire-and-forget event to Kafka; ClickHouse aggregates off the hot path
**Cache dies?** Misses fall to replicas; coalesce refills so one request fills each key; rewarm hot keys
**Make codes unguessable?** Random KGS keys, not sequential base62; 62^7 = 3.52T space; rate limit 404s
**Remove a link cached in CDN or browser?** Serve 302, or 301 with a short `max-age`; long 301s linger for months

blocks.note: short private max-age: clicks still reach you, expiry takes effect within 60 s

blocks.title: Cached redirects cannot be recalled
blocks.text: A 301 with a long `max-age` stays in browsers for ==months==. Delete or expire needs a **302** or a **short max-age** from day one.

rows: Browsers and CDN cache it; less load
Fresh link may 404 for under 1 s

blocks.text: Revision notes for the bit.ly-style **URL Shortener**: numbers, status codes, code generation, cache, analytics.

items: **7 chars** of base62 cover 6B URLs (5 years) with large headroom
Alert at ==50%== of 62^7 used

rows: Every click hits you: analytics, expiry
Browsers/CDN cache it; clicks are lost

items: Need every click or expiry → {green:302} (or 301 with a short private max-age)
Permanent 301 is hard to undo: it stays in browsers for months
{green:KGS}: pre-generated unique keys, API fetches batches of 1,000
{blue:Counter ranges}: each server gets a 1M-ID block, then base62
{orange:Hash}: first 7 chars of MD5/SHA-256 ==needs collision retry== (salt, rehash)
==Unique index on `short_code`== is the last guard; insert-or-fail, never check-then-insert
Target hit ratio ==above 95%==
**Negative cache** 404s for 60 s against random-code scans
**Coalesce** misses on a viral link: one request refills the key

blocks.title: Never block the redirect
blocks.text: Analytics is ==async== via Kafka. If Kafka is down, redirects still work and some clicks are dropped.

blocks.q: A counter hands out ID 3844 (that is 62 squared). With the alphabet 0-9, a-z, A-Z, what short code does base62 encoding produce? What does the next ID tell you about this scheme?
a_bullets: 3844 % 62 = 0, then 62 % 62 = 0, then 1 % 62 = 1; reversed, the remainders give `100`
Index 0 is '0' and index 1 is '1', so the code is `100`, which is 1x62^2
The next ID, 3845, encodes to `101`, so neighbouring codes are neighbouring links
Sequential base62 leaks creation order and volume, and anyone can guess other codes
If links are private, use a key service or random-looking codes instead

blocks.q: Spot the bug: a team serves every redirect as 301 with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000`. Later they notice click counts fall short and an expired link still opens for some users. Why?
a_bullets: Browsers and CDNs cache a 301, so repeat clicks never reach your server and are never counted
Your server's expiry check (410) never runs for those clients, because they skip the lookup
A wrongly cached permanent redirect stays in browsers for months and is hard to undo
Fix: use 302 (or 307), or a 301 with a short private max-age, when you need analytics and expiry

blocks.q: Spot the bug: two users submit the alias `summer` at the same moment. What can go wrong here, and what is the right fix?
a_bullets: Both requests can pass `exists` before either inserts, so check-then-insert is a race
Depending on the store, both get 201 and one link silently overwrites or duplicates the other
Fix: just insert, with a unique index on `short_code`, so the insert is atomic
The database lets one insert win; the loser gets a conflict and you return 409
The same unique index is the last guard for generated codes too

blocks.q: Spot the bug: the redirect handler waits for the click event to be published to Kafka before it sends the 302. Kafka has an outage. What do users see, and how should it be built?
a_bullets: Each redirect blocks on the publish, so redirects time out or fail even though the DB and cache are healthy
An analytics outage then breaks the core feature, and the read path loses its 99.99% availability
Fix: publish fire-and-forget into a bounded in-memory buffer, then send the 302 right away
When the buffer is full, drop events; losing some clicks is better than failing redirects
Watch the drop rate and the event lag (under 10 s) to know how much was lost

blocks.q: A user creates a link and clicks it a moment later, but gets a 404. Seconds later it works. Redirects are served from async read replicas. What happened and how do you fix it?
a_bullets: The write went to the primary, but the replica handling the click had not received it yet (replication lag)
The code was missing there, so the service returned 404 for a link that exists
Fix: read from the primary (or populate the cache on write) for a fresh link right after creation
Populating the cache on write also means the first click is a cache hit
Alert on replication lag (target under 1 s) to catch this early
